controls.prompt: Is the bass roll-off switch on? (When it is on, deep boomy sounds are cut and your voice sounds lighter.)

help.what: Cuts some deep bass, which helps with rumble and a boomy, close-up sound.

positions.label: Yes, it is on (lighter sound)
positions.meaning: Takes deep bass out, so your voice sounds lighter and cleaner.

controls.source: UNVERIFIED: general Shure SM7B knowledge, not confirmed from the manual

controls.prompt: Is the presence boost switch on? (When it is on, your voice sounds brighter and sharper.)

help.where: The other small switch under the same plate on the back of the mic (UNVERIFIED).

positions.label: Yes, it is on (brighter sound)
positions.meaning: Brighter, clearer speech; can make hissy sounds sharper.

controls.prompt: Is the little "bass tilt" switch on your mic switched on? (When it is on, your voice sounds thinner.)

help.what: This switch can thin out the deep bass on purpose, which helps if your voice sounds boomy or muddy.
help.where: A small up-and-down slide switch in a dark plate on the side of the mic body, between the ElectroVoice label and the black mount collar. Up (slanted line) is thinner sound; down (flat line) is normal.

positions.label: No, it is off (normal sound)
positions.meaning: Your natural, full sound. This is the normal setting.

positions.label: Yes, it is on (thinner sound)
positions.meaning: Takes some deep bass out, so a boomy voice sounds clearer but thinner.

controls.source: https://products.electrovoice.com/na/en/re20 and theaudacitytopodcast.com/re20 (one bass tilt-down switch). Location and icons confirmed from Otto's own photo of his RE20, 2026-11-06: small vertical slide switch in a dark plate on the side of the body between the label and the mount collar; slanted line at top = bass cut, flat line at bottom = normal. Position names not from the manual; verified flag unchanged

positions.label: Kick drum
